notes: STRONG, CONSISTENT SKILL EFFECT: with_skill = 1.00 across all 5 evals (perfect); baseline = 0.47 ± 0.08 (range 0.38-0.57). Delta +0.53 at a cost of only +13s and +12k tokens — cheaper overhead than solution-architect because base Claude already writes good architecture, so the skill mostly adds structure rather than net-new reasoning.

WHERE THE SKILL WINS IS STRUCTURE & PROCESS, NOT RAW TECHNICAL DEPTH: graders consistently noted the baseline's underlying engineering was as strong or (telehealth HIPAA, marketplace) arguably deeper. The skill's differentiation is the prescribed format — Source Breakdown, Constraints with [stated]/[assumed], Capability→Tech Mapping, ADR-style Key Architecture Decisions, depth marker, Research Suggestions with ready-to-use researcher queries, and the librarian handoff. Baseline produces equivalent content under ad-hoc headings and omits the ecosystem integrations entirely.

TWO GENUINE CONTENT WINS (not just headings): (1) baselines dropped whole stack layers — file-upload baseline omitted the frontend layer, subscription baseline omitted CI/CD — while the skill's comprehensive-stack requirement caught them. (2) subscription baseline FABRICATED an unstated constraint (claimed an existing user-account system and skipped auth); the skill correctly treated auth as to-provision and flagged the question. This validates the 'how not what / don't invent' discipline.

MISSING-BREAKDOWN BEHAVIOR IS A CLEAN DIFFERENTIATOR: given an under-specified prompt, the skill refused to fabricate, asked for the capability breakdown, tried librarian, suggested running solution-architect first, and asked 4 high-leverage questions. The baseline fired an exhaustive ~20-question requirements questionnaire — failing 'small number of targeted questions'. The skill's 'build on the breakdown' + 'interactive but light' principles both showed up in behavior.

EVAL QUALITY — known limitations flagged by graders: (a) Most assertions are heading/presence checks; they discriminate structure well but under-test technical correctness (e.g. the load-bearing 'scan-before-serve' sequencing is never asserted). Consider adding 1-2 substance assertions so the skill can't win on format alone. (b) The librarian/no-persist assertions are judged from prose only — no transcript was captured — so they can't verify an actual absence of a save. (c) 'Next Steps' is a strict heading match that fails the baseline's functionally-equivalent 'Implementation Roadmap' — a reward-outcome-vs-enforce-structure judgment call.

MISSING-BREAKDOWN EVAL has weak assertions worth tightening: 'retrieve via librarian OR ask the user' lets the generic ask-branch pass (split the librarian behavior into its own assertion); 'focus on high-leverage items' passes an exhaustive questionnaire that also fails 'small number of questions' (reword to require the questions be PRIMARILY the high-leverage few); 'does NOT persist' is vacuously true when no artifact is produced.

NO FLAKINESS OBSERVABLE at 1 run/config, but with_skill hit a clean 1.00 on every eval including the deep and constraint cases — strong signal. A 3-run consistency pass (like solution-architect iteration-2) would confirm reproducibility, especially on the deep marketplace eval where capability-count/structure has the most room to vary.
